title: Alpine Climbing
summary: The classic discipline: combining snow, ice and rock on high mountains, usually in a day or a few days, with minimal equipment and rapid movement. Ideal for objectives such as Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn and the great North Faces of the Alps.

title: Via Ferrata
tagline: Ladders, cables and iron in the rock
summary: Austrian and Italian mountain paths fitted with steel ladders, cables and anchors through steep terrain. Developed in the First World War for troop movement, now the most approachable way to experience serious alpine exposure safely.

title: Winter Mountaineering
tagline: The coldest season, the purest light
summary: Everything is harder and far quieter: spindrift, whiteouts and temperatures below -25 °C. Winter ascents are the ultimate expression of alpinism and demand the very best technical and psychological standards.
gradeSystem: Winter routes, plus extreme cold ratings

title: Big Wall
summary: Enormous faces climbed over weeks with fixed ropes, haul bags, porters and siege tactics. Big-wall climbing is as much a logistical art as a physical one, living and working on a hanging rope.

title: Rock Climbing
summary: From single-pitch sport crags to multi-day big walls. Rock climbing builds the footwork, balance and rope skills that underpin every other form of mountaineering, and is the best place to begin.

title: Ice Climbing
summary: Using ice axes and front-pointing crampons to climb frozen waterfalls, gullies and glaciers. A discipline of rhythm and precision that demands sound judgement of ice quality, temperature and avalanche exposure.

title: Expedition Style
summary: Long, logistically complex climbs on the world's greatest peaks: fixed ropes, staged camps, acclimatisation rotations and a team of guides and high-altitude support. Expeditions to peaks such as Denali, Aconcagua, Manaslu and Everest take three to nine weeks.

title: Bouldering
summary: Climbing short problems on boulders over crash pads. Bouldering concentrates on strength, technique and problem solving, and is a superb way to train finger strength and body tension for bigger objectives.

title: Trekking Peaks
summary: Non-technical or moderately technical peaks between 5,000 and 6,500 m that make perfect first Himalayan summits. Peaks such as Island Peak, Mera Peak and Lobuche East blend a classic trek with a real mountaineering objective.

title: Ski Mountaineering
tagline: Ascend on skins, descend in powder
summary: Travelling uphill on skis fitted with climbing skins, then descending untracked slopes. Ski mountaineering unites the freedom of the backcountry with serious alpine skills, and is also an Olympic sport from Milano Cortina 2026.
